title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GORDY'S BIG ROLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gordy Lindqvist, a fifty-two-year-old butcher in Missoula, Montana.
Gordy can cut a perfect steak with his eyes closed.
But ask him to talk in front of three people, and he turns the color of ground beef.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE TRYOUT
segments.quote: Always do what you are afraid to do.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: His wife Linda brought home a flyer. The town theater needed a Scrooge for A Christmas Carol.
Gordy said, absolutely not. Then he sat outside the tryouts in his truck.
On the dashboard, Linda had stuck a note from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Always do what you are afraid to do.
He walked in, read in a shaky voice, and got the part. He already looked grumpy.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LINES
segments.quote: The true art of memory is the art of attention.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: Scrooge had two hundred lines. Gordy forgot them by the time he hit the stairs.
The director, Maxine, gave him a line from the English writer Samuel Johnson:
The true art of memory is the art of attention.
So Gordy turned off the football game. He wrote his lines on butcher paper, and said them to the pork chops.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TOO MUCH
segments.quote: Suit the action to the word, the word to the action.
segments.author: William Shakespeare
lines: At rehearsal, Gordy played Scrooge like a cartoon villain. He growled. He nearly knocked over Tiny Tim.
Maxine sighed and read him Hamlet's advice to actors, from William Shakespeare:
Suit the action to the word, the word to the action.
So Gordy stopped shouting. Real grumpy is quiet. The room went still.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SCROOGE AT WORK
segments.quote: We are what we pretend to be, so we must be careful about what we pretend to be.
segments.author: Kurt Vonnegut
lines: But after six weeks of grumpy, Gordy snapped at Mateo, the young guy who stocks the cooler.
That night, Linda read him a line from the novelist Kurt Vonnegut:
We are what we pretend to be, so we must be careful about what we pretend to be.
Gordy said sorry to Mateo, with a bag of jerky. Then he practiced happy Scrooge at the counter. Customers loved it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: OPENING NIGHT
segments.quote: Against the assault of laughter nothing can stand.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: Opening night, the snow machine got stuck. Fake snow buried Gordy to his knees.
He froze. Then he remembered a line from Mark Twain:
Against the assault of laughter nothing can stand.
So Gordy laughed first. The whole crowd laughed with him. He shook off the snow and kept going.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: ALL YEAR
segments.quote: I will honor Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: In the last scene, Scrooge wakes up a new man.
Gordy said the line from Charles Dickens, and meant every word:
I will honor Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.
So he did. Every month, his counter sends soup bones to the food bank. And Mateo is trying out next year.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do the scary thing. Pay attention. Keep it real. Pretend well. Laugh first. Keep it all year.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do the scary thing. Pay attention. Keep it real. Be careful what you pretend. Laugh first. Keep the good stuff all year.
I was in a play once. I played a tree. I still forgot my line.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
